articles.title: Grecia - Países Bajos: horario y dónde ver en TV y online el partido de Nations League
articles.standfirst: Se enfrentan en la tercera jornada de Nations League
articles.summary: Se enfrentan en la tercera jornada de Nations League
articles.body: La selección de Grecia afronta el encuentro ante Países Bajos en un excelente momento de confianza, después de haber protagonizado uno de los resultados más destacados de las primeras jornadas de la UEFA Nations League. El combinado heleno, encuadrado en el Grupo A2, comenzó el torneo con una victoria por 1-2 frente a Serbia y confirmó sus buenas sensaciones al imponerse por 1-0 a Alemania en la segunda jornada, logrando así su primera victoria histórica ante los germanos. Con seis puntos de seis posibles, los griegos lideran el grupo y buscarán prolongar su buena dinámica ante otro de los grandes aspirantes. La solidez defensiva y la eficacia mostrada en sus primeros compromisos serán nuevamente sus principales argumentos para intentar conseguir un resultado positivo. Por su parte, Países Bajos llega a esta tercera jornada con la intención de asaltar el liderato y consolidar su candidatura en un grupo especialmente competitivo. El conjunto neerlandés, dirigido por Xavi Hernández, comenzó la competición con un empate por 1-1 ante Alemania, pero logró reaccionar en su segundo compromiso con una victoria por 2-1 frente a Serbia, gracias a un doblete de Mexx Meerdink. Con cuatro puntos en su casillero, la selección neerlandesa afronta una exigente visita a Grecia, donde necesitará mostrar su calidad técnica y capacidad ofensiva para superar a un rival que atraviesa un gran momento. El encuentro se presenta como una oportunidad importante para ambos combinados en la lucha por las primeras posiciones del grupo. El encuentro correspondiente a la Jornada 3 de la fase de grupos de la UEFA Nations League 2026/27 se disputa hoy, jueves 1 de octubre de 2026, a las 20:45 horas (hora peninsular española). El partido de la Liga de Naciones se podrá seguir en directo en España a través de DAZN y UEFA TV, según la programación de la jornada. Para conocer las alineaciones oficiales, seguir el minuto a minuto y disfrutar de toda la información de la previa y el análisis posterior, podrás consultar la cobertura deportiva online.

articles.title: Queiroz renuncia a la selección de Ghana
articles.standfirst: Llegó al cargo el pasado mes de abril de cara al Mundial
articles.summary: Llegó al cargo el pasado mes de abril de cara al Mundial
articles.body: La aventura de Carlos Queiroz al frente de la selección de Ghana, ahora ya de manera irrevocable, ha llegado a su fin tras apenas siete meses al frente del combinado nacional. "Tras conversaciones mantenidas en un espíritu de respeto mutuo, la Asociación de Fútbol de Ghana y yo hemos acordado mutuamente rescindir el Contrato de Servicios que rige mi función como entrenador de la Selección Nacional de Ghana", explicaba el propio Queiroz en su despedida. A sus 73 años, la federación de Ghana le contactó para que dirigiese a la selección en la que sería su quinta Copa del Mundo como seleccionador. Tras caer ante Colombia en los dieciseisavos de final, presentó su dimisión, volvió unas semanas más tarde... y ha vuelto a despedirse tras las derrotas cosechadas contra Costa de Marfil y Gambia en el proceso de clasificación a la próxima Copa África. "No fue una decisión fácil, pero ambas partes coincidimos en que, dadas las circunstancias actuales, poner fin a nuestra relación profesional era la medida más apropiada, anteponiendo los intereses de Ghana", reconoció Queiroz. "Ha sido un honor. Agradezco a la federación y al presidente por su confianza".

articles.title: Un once marcado por las bajas para el partidazo de Montilivi
articles.standfirst: El Girona tendrá más fondo de armario ante el Mallorca, otro de los 'candidatos', pero Quique Álvarez seguirá atado de manos
articles.summary: El Girona tendrá más fondo de armario ante el Mallorca, otro de los 'candidatos', pero Quique Álvarez seguirá atado de manos
articles.body: Las lesiones y los compromisos internacionales de media docena de sus futbolistas han dejado al Girona y a Quique Álvarez, su técnico, contra la espada y la pared. Por suerte blanquirroja, en el próximo partido contra el Mallorca, Bryan Gil y Fran Beltrán, este último muy justo de tiempo, podrían sentarse en el banquillo para ayudar en la segunda parte, además, parece que Pyshchur y Krapyvtsov, si no hay algún contratiempo de última hora, también podrían ampliar el fondo de armario. Y es que, si bien los dos lesionados que se recuperan no están, a priori, para ser titulares, los dos internacionales que llegan de un largo viaje lo harán el sábado, apenas 24 horas antes del partidazo. Si se añade que los futbolistas que vuelven liberados por el combinado Sub 21 de Ucrania no son jugadores titulares en los esquemas de su entrenador, todo apunta a que el Girona tenga que repetir el once que salió a jugar el último partido en Montilivi ante el Albacete formado por Gazzaniga, Boñar, David López, Francés, Alex Moreno, Izan, Morante, Carles Pérez, Van de Beek, Sarasa y Abel Ruiz. Además de los condicionantes y otros jugadores que no llegan en un buen momento físico, como Mumin, Unai o Portu, hombres como Jastin Garcia y Stuani siguen con los procesos de recuperación de sus respectivas lesiones musculares mientras que Asprilla, Vanat, Lass y, finalmente, también Holmes Junior, todavía están con sus selecciones y no podrán estar listos para el encuentro. Por otro lado, en el acuerdo de traspaso entre el Mallorca y el Girona por el lateral derecho Mateu Morey, según informó Última hora, el conjunto balear quiso poner una cláusula por la cual si el de Petra jugaba la presente campaña como rival, los gerundenses tenían que abonar una cantidad simbólica de dinero. El traspaso se cerró por poco más de 150.000 euros por lo que el dinero que deban pagar los blanquirrojos a los bermellones será también bajo. Morey precisamente debutó con el Girona en la última jornada ante el Albacete y, de momento, no ha podido hacerse con un lugar en el once por culpa del buen rendimiento en el lateral, primero de Francés y, últimamente, de Javi Boñar.

articles.title: Manchester City have the full set: 3 top Premier League dribblers now under the Etihad roof
articles.summary: If there’s one thing that feels totally at odds with a black-and-white, by the book, clinical team that operates on pure robotics rather than individual flai...
articles.body:
If there's one thing that feels totally at odds with a black-and-white, by the book, clinical team that operates on pure robotics rather than individual flair and creativity, it's players known for their dribbling. So, with Doku, Cherki, and Semenyo now all under the same roof – not to mention Illiman Ndaiye, another prolific dribbler on the pitch – is it finally time to retire the idea that Manchester City has computerised and mechanised its players into some sort of rigid formula that (often) trumps the more inventive, resourceful teams in the league? That isn't a view I agreed with, but it was prevalent during Pep Guardiola's decade as Manchester City manager.

Perhaps, although there will always be those who wrongly insist that Pep Guardiola's impressive record stems from one thing and one thing only: a decidedly unhuman, unbeautiful approach to the beautiful game that the rest of the footballing world wouldn't want anything to do with, even if it did produce six premier league titles in the space of one highly competitive decade. Not a view I agree with after watching some of the most breathtaking football seen in English football during Guardiola's decade kn charge of Manchester City. Still betting in the UK has long-since centred around the idea that Manchester City are here to plant balls in the net. Under Pep Guardiola, City did it while focusing on controlling matches which formed the backbone of the treble success during the 2022-23 season and much of their success under Guardiola.

There are similarities between Pep Guardiola's philosophy and that of Enzo Maresca. The start to the 2026-27 season has demonstrated some striking resemblances. Particularly when it comes to maintaining possession of the ball and maintaining relatively fixed positions on the pitch in a 3-2-2-3 shape of sorts with a full-back pushing into midfield, namely Josko Gvardiol, to provide attacking support.

Then again, among Manchester City's highest scorers were also the league's best dribblers. Last season, Doku and Cherki scored a respectable 9 goals between themselves in the Premier League. Rayan Cherki assisted the most of any Manchester City player in the Premier League, with 12. Doku ranked second for successful dribbles per 90 in the Premier League last season , and Cherki 9th, with 56.8% and 48.1% respectively. The choice to add Semenyo and then Ndaiye to the ranks – two players who are prolific at moving the ball across the pitch – seems to shed light on a preference for maintaining strength in transitional football, and reserving that ability to break through on dangerous counterattacks.

With Liverpool now practicing a higher press under Iraola, Manchester City having so many strong dribblers dangerous on the bounce could prove pivotal in the title race (If one including Manchester City eventuates after this week's events ). It may also be the only way to break down Arsenal's ever-strong defense.

This is something that Guardiola himself predicted: a growing emphasis on transitional styles over purely positional play. Looking at the evidence over the past few years' worth of signings, it would seem that the writing has been on the wall all along: diversify the philosophy, maintain rigid positional play and let the opponents start to forget that, behind it all, you have a dangerous penchant for sudden, intense attacks seemingly out of the blue.

Iliman Ndaiye's signing for Manchestwr City at the end of the summer transfer window signals exciting times ahead for The Citizens. Provided they can strike that ideal balance between control and creativity. It may just be enough for another winning season, even after the surprising loss of their long-time leader.

articles.title: Carlos Baleba expected to earn his first minutes for Man United this week in preparation for Tottenham Hotspur clash
articles.summary: 4Manchester United have a great opportunity to give fringe players and recently recovered stars valuable minutes ahead of the Premier League’s resumption fol...
articles.body:
Manchester United have a great opportunity to give fringe players and recently recovered stars valuable minutes ahead of the Premier League's resumption following the September international break.

The Red Devils are set to face fellow INEOS-owned outfit FC Lausanne-Sport this week in a behind-closed-doors friendly at Carrington.

Players who did not make the cut for their national teams, as well as academy graduates who are knocking on the first team door, are likely to get chances in the game.

Most importantly, Michael Carrick could turn to players who are on their way back from injury to assess how far along they are and whether they are ready to return against Tottenham Hotspur on 10 October.

Carlos Baleba to earn minutes vs FC Lausanne-Sport

Amad is one player who is pushing to play, as is Carlos Baleba, INEOS' costliest buy of the summer.

According to The Athletic , the ex-Brighton ace has recovered ahead of schedule, and his dedication has impressed coaches at Carrington.

There is a chance that the defensive midfielder will earn his first minutes against the Swiss side.

If the Cameroonian finishes the game unscathed, Carrick could finally hand him his United debut at Old Trafford against their North London rivals.

"Baleba, 22, has actually healed quicker than expected, which allowed him to be part of the matchday squad for the 1-1 draw at Fulham in the final game before players headed off with their countries. His work ethic has impressed staff.

"The midfielder was not deemed fit enough to be selected by Cameroon for their Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers in this window, given he has yet to play a minute this season, but could feature when a United academy side take on Lausanne-Sport of Switzerland later this week."

Carrick has badly missed the Cameroonian, with the midfield duo of Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo struggling to contain the opposition .

Carlos Baleba will inject energy and legs into the midfield and shield the leaky backline. That should also help improve United's abysmal fitness stats recorded so far this season.

articles.title: Ferguson on brain haemorrhage and games that shaped his life
articles.summary: Former Manchester United manager Sir Alex Ferguson speaks to BBC Breakfast as he approaches his 85th birthday.
articles.body:
"I was terrified," says Sir Alex Ferguson, one of the fiercest, most explosive and most decorated managers in football history.

The legendary former Manchester United boss is recalling the day he returned to Old Trafford for the first time after suffering a brain haemorrhage in May 2018.

Four months after emergency surgery, Ferguson - famous for his 'hairdryer treatment' when United dominated English football - was back to watch his beloved club take on Wolves in the Premier League.

The man responsible for making the dreams of United fans around the world come true for once was unsure of the reception he would receive from supporters.

"I wish I could say I was comfortable. I wasn't," Ferguson tells BBC Breakfast.

Ferguson and his wife Cathy received a standing ovation when they took their seats in the directors' box before kick-off.

"My wife was with me, and she was nearly crying. When we sat down, she said 'that's fantastic'."

Ferguson had been retired five years - after winning 38 trophies during 26 years in charge of United - at the time of his brain haemorrhage, aged 76.

Now three months short of 85, he says: "I'm feeling quite good despite small injuries."

The Scot has a new book coming out - 'Games of My Life'. It tells the stories of 21 defining matches in his playing and managerial career, revealing fresh insights into his journey from working-class Glasgow to dominating the English game - and Europe - as United boss.

Ferguson is thankful he is able to talk about the games that helped shape him.

"I had lost my voice; I couldn't speak," he says about the days immediately after brain surgery. "That was a frightening moment.

"I remember my grandsons coming to see me and I had lost my voice.

"Then they brought in a therapist and she started doing things like asking me to write down the names of birds, names of animals, names of rivers.

Ferguson won the lot during his time in charge of United between 1986 and 2013, including 13 Premier League titles.

He transformed them into a winning machine, and the history and tradition of United ran red through his veins.

As well as delivering two Champions League titles, Ferguson masterminded five FA Cup triumphs, won the League Cup four times and added the Club World Cup, European Super Cup, European Cup Winners' Cup and the Intercontinental Cup to the Old Trafford trophy cabinet.

In his book, Ferguson has picked standout games in his career, from winning his first cup final playing for Govan High School in Glasgow in 1955 at the age of 13 through to his retirement as a manager in 2013.

"That was my starting point," he says, holding the medal he received after that cup win 71 years ago.

"I played for Glasgow Schools, Scotland Schools and the Scotland youth team. The starting point of my career was there and I can look back with great satisfaction."

Ferguson describes growing up in Govan as "the making of me". He says he developed his inner confidence from his mother Elizabeth and a drive to succeed from his father Alexander, who worked in the Govan shipyards on the River Clyde.

"He was so proud of me and my brother," says Ferguson.

"He was a hard taskmaster because whenever I scored a hat-trick or a goal, my mother would say 'that's great, son'." His father, meanwhile, offered tough constructive criticism however many goals Ferguson had scored.

After making his debut as a 16-year-old striker for Queen's Park, Ferguson ended up at St Johnstone, where he endured a frustrating spell and nearly quit football for a new life in Canada.

"I wasn't enjoying it. I wasn't playing first-team football; I was in the reserves all the time," he says.

"I filled out all the forms and phoned my aunt in Canada, because you needed a sponsor then, and never told my mother and father."

The next day St Johnstone, decimated by a flu bug in the team, arrived at Ibrox to take on Rangers. A 21-year-old Ferguson was promoted to the starting XI and scored a hat-trick.

That life-changing performance in 1963 revived his playing career and set him on the path to becoming one of football's greatest managers.

"I would say this to young people - don't miss the biggest opportunity in your life. It's recognising it."

'Don't sell Ince to Inter - or you'll regret it'

Ferguson is sat in front of a table for the interview, which was conducted before the Premier League announced on Tuesday that Manchester City had been found guilty of all charges relating to breaches of financial regulations between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

On the table are several items from his career, including the Scotland cap he was finally presented with in 2021 - 54 years after appearing for his country.

Ferguson received the cap at Hampden Park on the night Scott McTominay - then a United player - scored a dramatic stoppage-time winner in a 3-2 win over Israel in a World Cup qualifier.

"I remember signing McTominay at seven years of age," Ferguson says.

Also on the table are old letters addressed to Ferguson from disgruntled United fans amid speculation he was about to sell midfielder Paul Ince to Inter Milan in the summer of 1995.

One reads: 'Don't sell Incey to Inter - or you'll regret it'. Another reads: 'Every Red is disgusted with you'.

"Paul was a tremendous footballer, there's no doubt about that," says Ferguson.

"He had incredible ability, but I just had that feeling that he just got carried away a bit at the time.

"He then got this offer from Inter Milan. I'm trying to weigh up one thing against the other. I'm looking at Paul Scholes and I said 'should we?'

"Milan's offer went from £7m to £7.5m and I said 'do it'.

"That's what your job is as a manager. You have to make hard decisions, and some decisions don't suit everyone."

There is also a notebook on the table with a list of words scribbled down by Ferguson when he used to address his players.

The names of Bernard "Monty" Montgomery, the World War Two general who outwitted his arch rival, and former prime minister Winston Churchill are on the list. So too is Ince.

"I didn't notice that before. I couldn't escape him," laughs Ferguson, who once called Ince a "big-time Charlie".

"I regret saying that. That was a mistake," Ferguson would later say.

"He's a good friend of mine," says Ferguson. "He used to come over and play snooker with me. He texted me not so long ago."

'Beckham thought I was trying to get rid'

"You can't win anything with kids," former Liverpool and Scotland defender Alan Hansen said after a youthful United side lost 3-1 at Aston Villa in August 1995.

Ince, 27, and forward Mark Hughes, 31, had been moved on in the summer to Inter and Chelsea respectively.

Meanwhile, Ryan Giggs, 21, Gary Neville, 20, Scholes, 20, and David Beckham, 20, were beginning to make a name for themselves.

By the end of the season, Ferguson's side had won the Premier League and FA Cup double.

"We'd worked really hard getting youth into the club again and this bunch of young lads became the spirit of Manchester United," says Ferguson.

"They added something. Apart from the great abilities they had, they had desire. I put Beckham out on loan at Preston [in March 1995] and he thought I was trying to get rid of him, which was not true.

"David was the last to really develop because of his physique. Although he grew to 6ft, he was small and thin as a young kid."

Did Ferguson ever fear that throwing his young players in at the deep end could backfire?

"I did exactly the same when I was in charge at St Mirren and Aberdeen," he says.

"I had belief in young people because if you give them an opportunity there are two things that happen - they become real stars and they can remain loyal to you as a manager."

articles.title: Los reyes de la Europa League rinden tributo a Antonio Puerta
articles.standfirst: El Sevilla se mide al Aston Villa en el regreso de Emery a Nervión casi cinco años después
articles.summary: El Sevilla se mide al Aston Villa en el regreso de Emery a Nervión casi cinco años después
articles.body: El Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán celebra este viernes (20:30 horas) una de las citas anuales más emotivas para todo el sevillismo. La XV Edición del Trofeo Antonio Puerta homenajea a la eterna zurda de diamante en un duelo de gran enjundia continental: el Sevilla de Luis García Plaza recibe al Aston Villa de Unai Emery en un choque que, más allá del componente sentimental, supone un examen de nivel para ambos. Asimismo, supone el regreso del técnico de Hondarribia a la que fue su casa y desde donde dio el gran salto a la élite del fútbol europeo. El nombre de Unai Emery está grabado con letras de oro en la historia del Sevilla. El entrenador de Hondarribia, que aterrizó en Nervión en enero de 2013 como relevo de Míchel, firmó una gesta inolvidable al conquistar tres títulos consecutivos de la Europa League (2014, 2015 y 2016). Después de su salida para poner rumbo al PSG, continuaría su idilio con esta competición añadiendo dos trofeos más a su palmarés, superando así al mítico Giovanni Trapattoni: primero lo hizo con el Villarreal (2021) y más recientemente con el propio Aston Villa (2026). Si bien Unai Emery y el Sevilla comparten una historia común más que exitosa, sus reencuentros con el Sánchez-Pizjuán no han sido nada plácidos sobre el césped. Esta será la tercera ocasión en la que el técnico vasco dirija desde el banquillo visitante tras su marcha en 2016. En las dos anteriores, ambas al mando del Villarreal, salió derrotado ante el conjunto que entrenaba el también ex sevillista Julen Lopetegui. En la jornada 16 de la temporada 2020-21, vencieron los hispalenses con goles de Lucas Ocampos y Youssef En-Nesyri (2-0); un año más tarde, en la misma fecha del campeonato, volvieron a imponerse gracias a otro tanto de Ocampos (1-0). En esta ocasión, el Aston Villa visita la capital hispalense después de completar un stage de concentración de tres días en Marbella. Los de Birmingham no han protagonizado un buen arranque en la Premier League, pues actualmente son decimosextos en la tabla con un triunfo, un empate y tres derrotas. Sin embargo, llegan en clara dinámica ascendente. En sus últimos dos partidos han logrado derrotar a domicilio al Coventry City en la EFL Cup (1-3) y al Tottenham Hotspur en la competición liguera (2-3). Mejor les ha ido en la Liga de Campeones, donde han ganado su único enfrentamiento ante el Brujas (2-3). Tanto Sevilla como Aston Villa afrontan este encuentro con varias ausencias, la mayoría provocadas por el parón de selecciones. Si los nervionenses no pueden contar con cinco futbolistas por este motivo, en el caso de los ingleses el número de internacionales asciende hasta nueve: Zion Suzuki, Matty Cash, Aaron Wan-Bissaka, Victor Lindelöf, Matteo Ruggeri, Johan Manzambi, John McGinn, Ibrahim Mbaye y Nicolas Jackson. Además, tampoco disponen por lesión de dos centrocampistas importantes como Amadou Onana y Leon Goretzka. Por parte del Sevilla, Luis García Plaza ha citado a 23 futbolistas, teniendo que convocar a varios jugadores del filial para paliar el virus FIFA. Al margen de los internacionales, en la lista no están ni Kike Salas ni Rubén Vargas, que ya han podido reincorporarse a los entrenamientos, ni tampoco Lucas Stassin, que sigue recuperándose de su lesión. Quienes sí integran finalmente la convocatoria son Fábio Cardoso, apartado del equipo hasta hace unos días, y Fran González, que también arrastraba molestias físicas. Esta XV Edición del Trofeo Antonio Puerta se presenta como una oportunidad para los futbolistas que vienen disponiendo de menos minutos (Carmona, Marcao, Julio Díaz, Manu Bueno, Alfon o Peque), así como para jóvenes con ganas de mostrarse ante su público (Rafa Romero, Loren, Mario Díaz, Nico Guillén, Manuel Ángel e Ibra Sow). Además, hombres importantes como Castrín o Fofana querrán aprovechar la ocasión para seguir ganando ritmo competitivo. Un test de altura ante un rival de Champions para calibrar sensaciones, poner a prueba conceptos tácticos y sobre todo rendir tributo a la memoria de Antonio Puerta junto a un técnico que hizo historia en Nervión.

articles.title: Samu habla claro sobre su salida del Atlético: "Pasaron muchas cosas que tampoco quiero contar"
articles.standfirst: El delantero repasa en La Tribu su dura recuperación, su regreso con el Oporto, su pasado en el Atlético y su objetivo de volver a la Selección
articles.summary: El delantero repasa en La Tribu su dura recuperación, su regreso con el Oporto, su pasado en el Atlético y su objetivo de volver a la Selección
articles.body: Samu Aghehowa vuelve a disfrutar del fútbol después de un largo periodo alejado de los terrenos de juego. El delantero atendió a Pablo Villa en La Tribu de Radio MARCA y repasó todo lo vivido durante su lesión, desde los momentos más complicados hasta la emoción de volver a sentirse futbolista. "La verdad que ha sido un camino muy largo. Gracias a Dios ha llegado a su fin", reconoció Samu, que pudo regresar en un partido especialmente importante para el Oporto: "La manera en la que me recibió el estadio fue increíble, algo que nunca se me va a olvidar". Una vuelta que incluso se produjo antes de lo esperado. "No estaba previsto para volver ese partido, pero al final todo fue como había soñado", explicó. Las buenas sensaciones durante las semanas anteriores permitieron adelantar su regreso: "Me veía muy bien entrenando y, hablando con los doctores, me pudieron dar el alta. Estaba todo bien". Samu no escondió la dureza de una recuperación que le obligó a vivir momentos completamente nuevos. "Hay días que no te apetece ni levantarte de la cama. Hay días que das un pasito y te sientes más cerca y, a lo mejor, al día siguiente no te sientes como tú pensabas que te ibas a sentir. Es un cúmulo de emociones". La lesión también cambió su manera de valorar el día a día: "Ahora valoro mucho más entrenar, jugar, estar con ellos. Es un aprendizaje que me llevo: valorizar cada momento que estás sano y que puedes disfrutar de lo que te gusta". El delantero también recordó las lágrimas tras conocer el alcance de la lesión. "Lo primero que pensé, no te voy a mentir, fue el Mundial", aseguró. Y volvió a emocionarse cuando finalmente regresó: "La última vez que lloré fue cuando terminó el partido, que volví a jugar. Al final es como una liberación de que ya ha pasado todo". Ahora sus sensaciones son completamente diferentes. "Cuando me veo entrenando, sinceramente, es como si no me hubiese lesionado. Incluso me siento mejor que antes", afirmó Samu, convencido de que los goles llegarán: "Estoy seguro de que va a ir todo bien, de que no voy a tardar mucho en marcar goles". Samu también habló de su etapa vinculada al Atlético de Madrid y de todo lo que ocurrió antes de marcharse. "Esta historia fue como una película. Yo lo viví muy intensamente porque al final me ficharon siendo nadie", explicó. Pese a todo lo sucedido, mantiene su agradecimiento hacia el club rojiblanco: "Estoy súper agradecido al Atlético. Yo prácticamente sin ellos a lo mejor no estaría donde estoy". Samu evitó profundizar en algunos episodios de aquella etapa: "Pasaron muchas cosas que tampoco quiero contar porque fue un periodo que lo pasé muy mal". "No tengo nada en contra de él", señaló sobre Simeone. "Es una lucha de intereses y creo que fueron cosas del pasado que al final uno olvida. Yo tampoco soy rencoroso", añadió. Otro de sus grandes retos es regresar a la Selección española. "Es un objetivo volver cuanto antes, estar en dinámica con ellos, poder disfrutar de esa selección", aseguró. Samu reconoce la dificultad, pero mantiene la confianza: "Sé que es complicado, pero confío mucho en mí. Sé que si hago las cosas bien tengo grandes posibilidades de volver". Por último, también se mojó sobre el Balón de Oro y señaló a su candidato: "Yo al final se lo daría a un español, pero particularmente se lo daría a Lamine porque al final es un jugador diferencial". Y dejó un elogio rotundo al futbolista del Barcelona: "Es un elegido. Tenemos la suerte de disfrutarlo en la selección y ojalá pueda llevárselo a casa".

articles.title: Henry: "En el fútbol, Zidane está a la altura de Dios"
articles.standfirst: "Cuando veías a Zizou en el banquillo del Real Madrid, estaba bastante tranquilo, sereno y efectivo. Incluso cuando Ronaldo marcó su chilena. Pero esto es la selección francesa...", dice Thierry en RMC
articles.summary: "Cuando veías a Zizou en el banquillo del Real Madrid, estaba bastante tranquilo, sereno y efectivo. Incluso cuando Ronaldo marcó su chilena. Pero esto es la selección francesa...", dice Thierry en RMC
articles.body: Zinedine está cumpliendo su sueño con su llegada al banquillo de la selección de Francia. "Me dije que la única cosa que quería hacer después del Real Madrid era esto", reconocía el míster, que esperó pacientemente a que se terminara la 'era Deschamps' para tener su oportunidad. Y ahora ya la está disfrutando. Pero él no es el único feliz. Muchos aguardaban con ansia el momento en el que se hiciera cargo de Les Bleus. Uno de ellos es Thierry Henry, que no escatima en elogios hacia el que durante su carrera fue su compañero en el combinado nacional. Ambos se proclamaron campeones del mundo en 1998. "La llegada de Zizou es algo extraordinario. Es tener a alguien que, en lo que al fútbol se refiere, está a la altura de Dios. Lo digo sin ánimo de ofender a los creyentes, pero para nosotros, en el fútbol, está a la altura de Dios", enfatizó Henry en el programa 'Rothen s’enflamme' de RMC. Zidane ha empezado con buen pie al frente de Les Bleus. Francia ha ganado los dos partidos en los que él ha estado en el banquillo. Firma un pleno: seis puntos de seis posibles. Las dos victorias han sido por la mínima. En el debut se impuso (0-1) a Turquía, el día que se lesionó Mbappé, que fue el autor del gol, y después derrotó a Bélgica, gracias a una acción espectacular de Olise. Esta noche disputará su tercer encuentro contra Italia. Además de la calidad, Henry destaca también la influencia que Zidane tiene sobre los jugadores. "Tenerlo en la selección francesa y ver lo que puede aportar a esta generación... Ya hemos visto a los chicos hablando y expresándose sobre él. Vimos cómo se les abrían los ojos... Es perfectamente normal porque, al fin y al cabo, ¡es Zizou! Pero aún necesitamos resultados, él ya ha conseguido algunos, y tendrá que mantenerlos. Así que, como dije sobre Deschamps, ¡mucha suerte!", afirmó. Henry, por otro lado, explica la carga emocional que supone para un profesional estar en la selección gala. "Habéis visto bien la reacción de Zizou al gol de Michael Olise, eso lo hace el gallo [referencia al símbolo de la selección francesa]. Hay algo diferente y, sin embargo, estamos hablando de Dios, estamos hablando de él: lo ha hecho todo. Pero volver a Clairefontaine, volver a la selección francesa...", dice y lo compara con la actitud de Zizou en su etapa en el Santiago Bernabéu: "Cuando veías a Zidane en el banquillo del Real Madrid, estaba bastante tranquilo, sereno y efectivo. Incluso cuando Ronaldo marcó su chilena. Pero esto es la selección francesa...".

articles.title: German football: The leagues where champions aren't promoted
articles.summary: German football is grappling with a sum that doesn't add up - four promotion spots for five league champions.
articles.body:
Djamal Ziane is a three-time league champion – but he does not always feel like it.

This summer, for the second year in a row and for the third time in seven seasons, the Lokomotive Leipzig captain hoisted the trophy into the air having led his team to the title in the Regional League Northeast, the fourth tier of German football.

But the memory is tinged with frustration because, just as in 2025 and 2020, Lokomotive's league title did not lead to promotion.

While the other regional champions in the German fourth division were promoted to the nationwide 3. Liga, "Lok" faced a play-off against a representative of the Regional League Bavaria, Wurzburger Kickers. Ziane scored, but an injury-ravaged Leipzig lost 3-1 on aggregate.

"Euer System ist krank," read a simple protest banner displayed by the 2,000 travelling supporters – "your system is sick".

"It's the worst thing – injury aside – that you can experience as a footballer," Ziane tells BBC Sport.

"Catastrophe doesn't cut it. It doesn't make any sense. If they really wanted to change it, they could do tomorrow."

Germany's football pyramid has a bottleneck.

Beneath the Bundesliga, 2. Bundesliga and 3. Liga, the fourth tier is split into five regional divisions (North, West, Southwest, Northeast and Bavaria), each of which produces a league champion.

So far, so good. But with only four teams being relegated from the 3. Liga each season, the sums don't add up.

An unsatisfactory solution is currently in place: the champions in the West and Southwest go up automatically while a third automatic promotion spot is rotated among the other three leagues in a three-year cycle. The fourth spot is allocated via a play-off between the winners of the remaining two leagues.

One champion always misses out and, increasingly, it's the champion from the Regional League Northeast, covering the territory of the former eastern German Democratic Republic (GDR).

In addition to Lok Leipzig's triple tragedy, former serial GDR Oberliga winners Dynamo Berlin fell short in 2022 and Energie Cottbus drew the short straw in 2023. This season, there is only one eastern German club in the 3. Liga: Hansa Rostock.

The struggles of the regions' football clubs are, to some degree, a result of continuing socio-economic disparities between east and west, which were also reflected in the success of the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party in recent state elections.

Even in 2026, not one of the 40 leading companies listed on Germany's DAX stock exchange is based in the former east (outside Berlin). Salaries remain lower, unemployment remains higher and the population is older and shrinking as young people move west.

The reason that automatic promotion spots are handed to the champions in the West and Southwest is simply because there are more men's football teams registered in those jurisdictions - because more people live there.

It is an argument that Ziane is tired of hearing.

"In that case, you might as well give us the automatic promotion spot because we attract bigger crowds," he says.

Indeed, the average attendance in the Regional League Northeast last season (3,125) was around twice as high as that in the other leagues. Lok Leipzig themselves had the fourth highest (6,352). More than 11,000 attended the local derby against city rivals Chemie Leipzig.

"Unfortunately, you don't get any points for tradition, crowds and history," says 39-year-old Lok chief executive Toni Wachsmuth, who does not have access to sponsors with the same financial firepower as his counterparts further west.

"The [western] leagues do have better economic foundations but everyone agrees that the current system is nonsense. Everyone needs to compromise but some officials are clearly putting their own interests and positions above the general good of German football."

It comes as little surprise, therefore, that the latest push for change has come from the east, with clubs launching a new campaign in March 2025 with the slogan: "Meister mussen aufsteigen!" – champions must go up!

Their proposal: a reduction from five leagues to four, with the precise geographical borders to be determined anew each season with the help of artificial intelligence, taking into account factors such as distance of travel to away games and attractive derbies.

They call it the compass model. Because it can go in all directions. In return, the Regional League Northeast is prepared to compromise by giving up its emotional attachment to the territory of the former East Germany.

"I want to get away from this east-west debate," says Tommy Haeder, the 35-year-old chief executive of Chemnitzer FC and figurehead of the reform campaign. "We've had a change of generation. Many older officials have retired and been replaced by younger people who don't have this nostalgia for the GDR."

Haeder also emphasises the benefits that a fairer promotion system would bring for German football as a whole, arguing that eastern clubs would be better equipped to continue nurturing youth talent.

"It's not in the interest of talent development when young footballers from Chemnitz are torn away from their homes and families at the age of 10 to join academies in Hamburg, Dortmund or Stuttgart," he tells BBC Sport.

"The compass model is a model in which every region sacrifices a little bit to solve a much bigger problem. We're organised, we have a plan, we've made suggestions. Now it's up to the federations to act."

The campaign has since gained the support of more than 80 clubs across Germany, from east to west and up and down the pyramid.

Union Berlin, who were playing in the fourth tier as recently as the 2000s, became the first Bundesliga club to officially back the initiative, with club president Dirk Zingler saying: "The current set-up contradicts our understanding of sporting competition."

Borussia Dortmund president – and Bundesliga chairman – Hans-Joachim Watzke added his influential voice, stating: "Champions must go up and we think the compass model with four regional leagues is the best option."

Support also has also come from Bournemouth head coach Marco Rose who, drawing on his past as both a player and coach at Lok Leipzig, said: "I know what it's like for clubs trying to work within their means, or lack of means, at that level. Everything is on a knife edge.

"You have to give the clubs and their fans the belief that their efforts and sacrifices will be rewarded with promotion."

Momentum was growing before a key vote at the end of June when, after months of discussions, clubs were finally set to vote on the compass model – but the ballot descended into farce when, at the last minute, the regional federations conducting the vote announced two key changes:

Suddenly, the four new leagues would consist of only 18 teams rather than 20 (thus making the compass model less attractive because 10 more teams would miss out), and a stipulation was added that a majority be reached in each of the five regions for the model to pass.

An overall majority (50.9%) in favour of the compass model was still reached (including 60.9% in the West, 61.5% in the North and 76.3% in the Northeast) but the Southwest voted for an alternative option in which the northeastern league would be dissolved and its clubs reallocated, while the Southwest and West would simply remain the same.

"The move from a functioning system to a complex, insecure and economically riskier model without an obvious benefit doesn't make any sense to me," Robert Lempka, chief executive of Regional League Southwest side FSV Frankfurt told local public broadcaster Hessischer Rundfunk this summer. "I find it unsettling that an untransparent algorithm should decide a club's future."

The Bavarians, meanwhile, voted vaguely for "further talks", with Bavarian Football Federation (BFV) President Christoph Kern telling Munich's Abendzeitung newspaper in August: "We've gathered our clubs together on several occasions and none of the suggested models have majority support. I'm not prepared to simply give up the Regional League Bavaria like that."

For Haeder in Chemnitz, the vote was "an absolute catastrophe – completely amateurish". And he's not alone.

This season, protests have erupted across German football. In the Regional League Northeast, almost every game has begun with a delay as players have simply refused to play for the first minute.

On the opening day, Lok Leipzig supporters, their team still stranded in the same division, threw hundreds of plastic trophies on to the pitch, symbolising the worthlessness of their club's back-to-back titles.

Down in Bavaria, Bayern Munich's ultras attended a reserve team game in the regional league and produced an intricate choreography criticising the Bavarian Football Federation (BFV) for what they perceive to be an unco-operative stance.

"You've taken us for fools long enough," read a banner beneath a display depicting BFV officials using a magnet to pull a compass needle towards them. The ultras then set off red pyrotechnics which turned the compass needle back in the direction of the fans.

And before the international break, fans of clubs across the Bundesliga used their platform to call for reform with co-ordinated banners reading: "Clubs and fans betrayed! Champions must go up! Compass model now!"

The compass, it would appear, may finally be pointing towards a resolution after the German Football Federation (DFB) announced the convening of an extraordinary general meeting on 18 December.

"[The issue] must be resolved," said President Bernd Neuendorf. "The compass model received the most votes and offers the best chance for a concentration of elite performance and therefore better development of talent."

Any changes would only be implemented in the 2028-29 season – too late for Ziane who, now 34, has embarked on his 13th season with Lok Leipzig. Back-to-back champions, but still in the fourth division.

"You can never completely get over it because, at our level, the 3. Liga is probably the pinnacle. Promotion with my hometown club would have been the most wonderful thing in the world for me," he says before heading out for training.

"It's a shame that we have to force ourselves to remember what we've achieved. It's so hard to win this league and we did it twice in a row! You can't take that for granted."

articles.title: Republic of Ireland 2-2 Austria: Hallgrimsson marvels at 'magical' Parrott's solo goal
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson praises Troy Parrott after his fine solo goal in their 2-2 Uefa Nations League draw against Austria on Thursday.
articles.body:
"There aren't many players that can do what he did."

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson succinctly summarised the brilliance of in-form striker Troy Parrott for his first goal in their Uefa Nations League 2-2 draw with Austria in Dublin.

Having been fed the ball by Adam Idah around 20 yards from goal, Parrott stalled for a second and even gestured for support around him before deciding to go alone.

First, he nutmegged Philipp Lienhart, then he sidestepped his defensive partner David Affengruber before showing why Real Betis paid big money for him in the summer by slotting through goalkeeper Florian Wiegele's legs.

His team-mate Jack Moylan's reaction mirrored that of many supporters in the stands after the ball hit the net, with the Cardiff City man standing with his hands on his head in disbelief but with a huge smile that showed his glee after witnessing such a special goal.

It was one of the finest goals scored at the Aviva Stadium and one that Hallgrimsson said will be replayed "again and again for many years to come".

While his last-gasp winner that completed his hat-trick against Hungary and secured a World Cup play-off in November last year may be his most memorable goal, there is no doubting that this was the best of an ever-growing catalogue in a green shirt.

Parrott then doubled his and his side's advantage when he kept his cool to tuck home a penalty on the stroke of half-time to take his tally to 14 in 40 caps, with nine of those coming in his last six competitive games.

That looked to have set the Irish on their way to back-to-back wins after he also found the net in the victory against Israel on Sunday, but Austria fought back, scoring shortly before he was substituted on 75 minutes and then finding a second soon after to earn a point.

"It was just a shame it was not a goal that gave us a win but I think you will be watching it anyway for years to come," Hallgrimsson added.

The result tainted a fine personal night for Parrott, but given the trajectory he is on, there are set to be many more to come.

Republic of Ireland and Austria draw in game briefly halted by protests

Parrott, who also has two goals and an assist in limited minutes at his new club Betis this season, has the chance to continue his nearly year-long hot streak for his country on Sunday as Republic of Ireland face Israel again in Serbia to close a gruelling four-game international break.

Hallgrimsson explained after the Austria game that part of the thinking behind substituting the tiring striker for speedster Chiedozie Ogbene, despite the fact he was on a hat-trick, was to ensure he would be fresh and raring to go again for that game in Backa Topola.

After all, Parrott, along with Idah and Moylan who he linked up well with on Thursday again, were key in the comfortable 3-0 win against Israel in the first game in Hungary.

Another win against the same opposition would move Republic of Ireland onto seven points and would give them a good chance of finishing second and securing a place in pot two for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw heading into November's final two games away to Austria and at home to Kosovo.

"Absolutely not," Hallgrimsson replied when asked if he regretted bringing Parrott off in Dublin.

"He had a few knocks and he was getting tired and we need him in three days. I've always said about Troy, I know he has a special gift going forward and scoring goals but what I always see in him that I don't see in many other attackers is his defensive discipline and hard work," he continued.

"I hope he continues to improve, but it is magical for Irish football to have him in a green shirt."

articles.title: El derbi del perdón
articles.standfirst: El regreso de Cestero tras el castigo centra la atención del duelo de filiales de hoy en el Di Stéfano (21.15 horas)
articles.summary: El regreso de Cestero tras el castigo centra la atención del duelo de filiales de hoy en el Di Stéfano (21.15 horas)
articles.body: El Di Stéfano será hoy el escenario del derbi del perdón. Castilla y Atlético Madrileño se enfrentan en Valdebebas (21.15 horas, Orange TV, Movistar Primera Federación y Dazn) en un duelo de filiales marcado por el regreso de Cestero a la convocatoria. El Madrid ha levantado el castigo impuesto a su canterano tras un desencuentro con el entrenador y el centrocampista se apunta al duelo ante los rojiblancos. Ahora sólo queda saber si su vuelta es directa al once (era titularísimo para Julián López de Lerma antes de la polémica) o si estará en el banquillo. El que también estará presente en el derbi de filiales es Thiago Pitarch, que se mantiene en la dinámica del Castilla para seguir acumulando minutos aprovechando el parón del primer equipo. El Castilla recibe a los rojiblancos en apuros, tras encadenar tres partidos sin ganar, con una sola victoria en las cinco primeras jornadas y en una incómoda e inesperada decimocuarta posición, tras un balance de una victoria, dos derrotas y dos empates. Será el tercer derbi en 13 días entre los tres primeros equipos de Real Madrid y Atlético, con dos triunfos ya para los rojiblancos. Lo que empezó Simeone (2-1 en el Metropolitano) y continuó Manuel Ruano ( Atlético C 2-0 Madrid C), lo puede terminar hoy Fernando Torres. El técnico del Atlético Madrileño puede cerrar el círculo de un triplete de derbis para los rojiblancos. Será el undécimo derbi de Torres como técnico, con un balance de tres victorias, cuatro empates y tres derrotas. Además, será su segunda visita. Además, será su sexta cita en Valdebebas como entrenador. En las cinco anteriores, cosecha dos victorias, dos empates y una derrota. Fernando Torres se vuelve a ver las caras con los madridistas tras una temporada pasada en la que no hubo derbi al estar en distintos grupos.

articles.title: Sir Alex Ferguson: Former Manchester United boss admits he was 'terrified' about making Old Trafford return after 2018 brain haemorrhage
articles.summary: Sir Alex Ferguson underwent emergency surgery for a brain haemorrhage in 2018; Manchester United's most decorated manager returned to Old Trafford less than four months later after fearing he would lose his voice
articles.body:
Manchester United's most decorated manager underwent emergency surgery after falling ill in May 2018, and was placed in intensive care at Salford Royal Hospital.

Speaking in 2021, Ferguson admitted that he feared losing his memory and his ability to speak, but has now revealed his emotions ahead of his return to the director's box at the Theatre of Dreams.

The Scot was in attendance for United's 1-1 draw with Wolves, less than four months on from being admitted to hospital, and told BBC Breakfast that he was unsure what the response from fans would be towards him.

"I was terrified. I wish I could say I was comfortable. I wasn't," Ferguson said.

"I didn't know what the reaction was [going to be]. Then they make the announcement and then of course there was a loud applause.

"My wife was with me, and she was nearly crying. When we sat down, she said 'that's fantastic'.

"It's one of those things. That's the generosity of our support and recognising my time there."

Ferguson, now 84, is still a regular fixture at Old Trafford for Manchester United matches, and also revealed that he was in good health considering what he went through.

"I'm feeling quite good despite small injuries," he added.

"I had lost my voice; I couldn't speak. That was a frightening moment.

"I remember my grandsons coming to see me and I had lost my voice.

"Then they brought in a therapist and she started doing things like asking me to write down the names of birds, names of animals, names of rivers. That way my voice came back."

articles.title: España estrenará en Croacia la camiseta blanca con dos estrellas
articles.standfirst: Y en noviembre jugará con ella en Praga
articles.summary: Y en noviembre jugará con ella en Praga
articles.body: La camiseta blanca, la segunda equipación de España, se ha convertido en uno de los mayores éxitos de la historia de Adidas. Su impacto desde el momento de su lanzamiento, el pasado mes de marzo, desbordó las previsiones. En Split, el próximo martes, España jugará con la camiseta blanca. En la visita a Croacia será la primera vez que la selección aparezca de blanco y con las dos estrellas encima del escudo. El último partido de España con esa camiseta y una sola estrella fue la semifinal del Mundial, ante Francia en Dallas. Después de jugar los tres primeros partidos de esta Liga de las Naciones de rojo, España lo hará de blanco en los dos siguientes. Porque en Praga, el 12 de noviembre, le tocará cambiar de color al ser el rojo el de la primera equipación de los checos. Hasta ahora, la selección española ha jugado cinco partidos con la camiseta blanca y en todos ellos ha dejado su meta a cero. En los amistosos de marzo ganó 3-0 a Serbia y empató sin goles ante Egipto. En la Copa del Mundo fueron tres partidos de blanco: Uruguay (1-0), Bélgica (1-0) y Francia (2-0). Con la camiseta blanca, igual que con la roja, el máximo goleador desde marzo es Mikel Oyarzabal. Suyos fueron dos de los tres goles ante Serbia en La Cerámica y el de penalti ante Francia que abrió el camino a la final y a la gloria.

articles.title: FA Cup: 'Hitchy is always with us' - remembering Barton Town keeper James Hitchcock
articles.summary: The memory of James Hitchcock lives on at non-league Barton Town, almost two years after he died following being punched on a visit to York.
articles.body:
"Even now, more than 18 months on, it has still not fully sunk in. I see little Freddie growing up and it hits me so hard."

Chris Hitchcock is talking about the loss of his son James, a goalkeeper for non-league Barton Town, who died after a single punch to the head in an unprovoked attack.

James, a popular team-mate known as 'Hitchy' to family and friends, was killed in December 2024, just before he was about to spend his first Christmas as a father following the birth of Freddie six months earlier.

His death not only devastated his family, it left a tight-knit football club in mourning.

"Until you start speaking about it again... it almost doesn't feel real," says Anthony Bowsley, manager of Lincolnshire part-timers Barton.

The day before the attack, James had pulled off a fine save in a 1-1 draw with Bottesford Town in the Northern Counties East League Premier Division.

"As he was coming off, I said to him 'great save Nigel Martyn' because Hitchy was a Leeds fan and he had a little chuckle to himself," says Bowsley.

The following day, the former Leeds United academy player, 32, was struck from behind at York Railway Station on his way back from a day out with friends. He died in hospital.

On Saturday, his widow, April, and son Freddie, now aged two, will be at Barton Town's FA Cup third qualifying round home tie with Chorley - one of the biggest matches in the ninth-tier club's history.

April, who married James in July 2022, says being around the football club where he used to play brings comfort after the unimaginable loss of her husband.

"It's really sad looking at where James used to stand in goal and saying 'where is he?'" April, 32, tells BBC Sport.

"It was a numb feeling. You don't believe something like that could happen to one of your mates," Barton Town defender Jack Bulless says.

Bulless, who also played with James at Bridlington Town, should have been part of the group on the day trip to York but pulled out due to illness.

Andy Norfolk, a long-time friend and team-mate, did join James and their friends.

"I remember the Manchester derby being on television in the bars we visited," says Norfolk.

"It was an annual Christmas get-together, a day trip, nothing too heavy. We arrived back at the station to go home early.

"I ended up getting a taxi back to Hull as the train was not for another hour. I remember Hitchy saying he was going to get some food."

It was the last time Norfolk saw his friend.

Leeds Crown Court heard James suffered a fracture to his skull and brain damage when he fell to the floor after being punched on the right side of the back of his head.

Recalling that day, April says: "I'd just put Freddie to bed when I got a call to say James had been hit, that he was unconscious, and was on his way to hospital.

"At that point I thought he had concussion and I needed to pack a bag because he was only going to be in for a day or two.

"When I got to the hospital they explained that he needed to be transferred to the intensive care unit at Hull Royal Infirmary. He was on a life support machine until he lost the battle."

Mckenzie Dicicco, who was then 22, was jailed for six years and eight months in July 2025 after pleading guilty to manslaughter for what judge Guy Kearl said was a "cowardly, deliberate and vicious attack on a man who had no chance to defend or brace himself".

Speaking after the verdict, April described being "lost and alone as the love of my life was so selfishly taken from me".

James' father, Chris, who used to take his son to Elland Road to watch David O'Leary's Leeds team in the late 90s, says his life has changed forever because of "one senseless act".

"I don't live any more - I exist," he says.

"I try and be happy, I try and do things and I put a brave face on. But it'll never be the same again for me."

James' memory lives on at Barton Town, whose 3,000-capacity ground is within eyeshot of the Humber Bridge.

"He is always with us," says Bowsley, referring to 'Hitchy #1' which has been sewn on to the back of the club's shirts.

"It's a beautiful thing to have on the shirt," adds Norfolk, who attended his friend's stag do in Benidorm, wedding near York and then his funeral - all in the space of two and a half years.

"Before each game I look at the back of the shirt and have my 10 seconds with Hitchy before I put it on."

There is also a plaque at the entrance to the players' tunnel in memory of James.

In addition, his two former clubs - Bridlington Town and Barton Town - meet annually for the James Hitchcock Memorial Trophy to raise funds for the Victim Support National Homicide Service.

Stories about James are frequently told in the club house.

"You could hear him before you saw him because of his distinctive laugh," adds Bulless.

Norfolk agrees. "His laugh was outrageously infectious. We all used to call it a cackle."

Meanwhile, Bowsley says James "always had a smile on his face" and was "a bit of a practical joker."

Talking about his ability as a goalkeeper, Bowsley adds: "He was a really good shot stopper and really good with his feet. He was at Leeds academy and then played the local leagues in Hull before going to Bridlington and then Barton."

Bulless adds: "He always had a way at making you laugh. There's always a couple of bags of sweets in the changing room, but Hitchy would always have his own bag.

"He wouldn't tell anyone he had them. Then you'd hear the packet rattling just as the manager was trying to deliver a team talk - or was about to give a player a dressing down.

"Hitchy would be sat in the corner making all this noise eating a bag of sweets."

James' dad used to be a non-league referee but stopped so he could travel to watch his son play when he became semi-professional.

"I used to go to the Lake District, Newcastle, you name it," says Chris. "I loved watching James play.

"He loved football from the first time he picked a ball up aged two or three. He never put it down. He just loved the game."

Since James' death, Chris has returned to officiating matches and was an assistant referee for Barton's FA Cup tie with North Ferriby earlier this season.

"When James left us I thought, 'right, what used to take my mind off things many years ago?'. It was refereeing and that's what I went back to.

"It's hard work at my age, but it does help when what's happened is constantly on your mind."

Meanwhile, April continues to keep James' memory alive.

"He was just lovable," she says about the man she met through mutual friends 12 years ago.

"He always had a smile on his face and had an infectious laugh. James lit up a room and he had so many friends who became part of our lives, part of our routine.

"When something like this happens, connections really form. We're really fortunate because the football community and Barton Town, they've not forgotten about James.

"Everybody gets on with their lives and everybody moves on.

"But for me the football community, especially Barton Town, have been like: 'let's do stuff, let's get you involved'.

'They asked if it was ok if they put James' name on the back of their shirts.

"Keeping his memory alive just speaks volumes. They were such a close group of friends.

"Freddie and I are fortunate that we haven't lost that - and they've not lost touch with us either.

"I take Freddie with me to matches. I want to raise my little boy in a world where he knows about his dad.

"I want to make sure he is involved as much as his dad was."

articles.title: "¿Entonces Mbappé no puede salir de la cueva hasta que el Madrid gane un título?"
articles.standfirst: Pepe Pasqués analiza el momento del jugador francés después de las imágenes del futbolista junto a su pareja en París
articles.summary: Pepe Pasqués analiza el momento del jugador francés después de las imágenes del futbolista junto a su pareja en París
articles.body: María José Hostalrich, Luz Monzón, Pepe Pasqués, Javi Lázaro, José Manuel Oliván y Nacho Labarga han sido los tertulianos de este viernes en La Tribu, patrocinada por Sportium durante esta temporada, para analizar la actualidad deportiva marcada por el tema el Caso Negreira, la situación de Mbappé o todo lo ocurrido con Cristiano Ronaldo y la selección de Portugal. María José Hostalrich. "Cuando su entrenador mismo dijo sobre todo jugador "aquí se es jugador del Real Madrid 24/7 lo dijo por algo. La torpeza es sobresaliente". Luz Monzón. "Es totalmente inapropiado y no está aceptado, pero por lo que he hablado con especialistas Esther Expósito genera muchas veces más como marca que él y a lo mejor el foco no es él porque ella tiene una marca más potente que él, es una de las marcas más relevantes a nivel mundial. No te digo que no salgas, pero hay que ser inteligente". Pepe Pasqués. "Ha marcado 94 goles en 111 partidos, el equipo no ha ganado nada... Entonces, ¿qué hace, no sale de la cueva hasta que el equipo gane un título?" Nacho Labarga. "Se equivoca en este tipo de situaciones, pero yo creo que a Mbappé ya le da igual lo que opine la gente o lo que escriban, las fotos... No tiene ninguna discreción, los jugadores si quieren que no se les vea no se les ve". José Manuel Oliván. "El problema es que Mbappé está lesionado y eso no queda bonito de cara a su afición y tampoco con la afición francesa". Javi Lázaro. "En 111 partido ha hecho 94 goles y tiene a la gente enfadada... Elcaldo de cultivo que hay alrededor de Mbappé es preocupante. Alguien debe de estar preocupado porque cada vez que saca medio pie le caen unos palos...".

articles.title: Portugal cierra filas: "Me han dicho que no puedo hablar de Cristiano"
articles.standfirst: "Es un asunto que no nos incumbe. Hemos demostrado que somos un gran grupo. Seguro que él, en casa, está contento por la victoria", dijo Leao
articles.summary: "Es un asunto que no nos incumbe. Hemos demostrado que somos un gran grupo. Seguro que él, en casa, está contento por la victoria", dijo Leao
articles.body: Portugal cierra filas. Tras el terremoto provocado por el abandono de la concentración de Cristiano Ronaldo, el cuerpo técnico, con Jorge Jesus al frente, y los jugadores miran hacia adelante e intentan 'olvidar' lo ocurrido. Todos dan valor al triunfo ante Dinamarca, el primero sin CR7, y prefieren pasar de puntillas por el conflicto. "Lo más importante es que el equipo cree en lo que hace", dijo tras el partido el seleccionador portugués, que esquivó en la rueda de prensa varias preguntas vinculadas a lo ocurrido la víspera. La única referencia a Cristiano la hizo en declaraciones a pie de campo a la televisión pública portuguesa RTP antes del encuentro en el Parken de Copenhague. "Explicaré todo después del último partido. Llevo muchos años en el fútbol y sé que no hice nada que debería haber causado que las cosas fueran diferentes. Hablaremos de este tema. No me esconderé ni huiré de él", dijo. Pero, por ahora, prefirió guardar silencio. Renato Veiga tampoco se explayó sobre la situación de Cristiano, pero sí desveló cuál es la política de comunicación que se ha instaurado en el seno de la selección. "Soy muy cercano a Cris, él sabe que le tengo mucho cariño, pero me han dicho que no puedo hablar de él", afirmó. Nuno Mendes, al ser cuestionado por CR7 y por cómo afectó su marcha, se centró sólo en el fútbol. "Obviamente, Cristiano es jugador de la selección nacional. Estamos más concentrados en lo que tenemos que hacer ahora y en el próximo partido, en ganar en el Estadio do Dragao. Estamos enfocados en el fútbol. Eso es lo que el entrenador nos ha enseñado y lo que nos transmite. Solo podemos jugar, el resto no depende de nosotros. Estamos aquí para recibir a cualquiera, sea quien sea. No, no nos afectó. Estamos enfocados en el fútbol. Lo que hicimos hoy fue muy importante", indicó. "Es un asunto que no nos incumbe. Hemos demostrado que somos un gran grupo. Seguro que él, en casa, está contento por la victoria. Como compañero de equipo, sé cómo es. Lo más importante es el equipo y ahora hay que descansar y prepararse para el partido", comentó, por su parte, Leao, que heredó el dorsal 7 de CR7 para el encuentro ante Dinamarca: "Ha sido muy especial. Cristiano es un ídolo para mí, y el número siete también tiene un significado especial, ya que es la fecha de nacimiento de mis hijos. He intentado disfrutarlo con mis compañeros y lo más importante es haber hecho un buen partido". A Vitinha también le cuestionaron por Cristiano. "¿Pudieron mantenerse al margen de todo lo que sucedió?", le preguntaron. "Sí, intentamos concentrarnos en el partido y lo conseguimos. Creo que respondimos de maravilla y felicito a todo el equipo por ello", dijo. Jorge Jesus también quiso rebajar el clima de tensión que se ha generado en las últimas horas en torno a la selección de Portugal. "Nadie puede quitar lo que Cristiano representa. Es un icono y eso no es algo que se pueda debatir", terminó el seleccionador. En los próximos días, todos volverán a hablar del 'caso Cristiano'. Seguro...

articles.title: El gran traspaso que se cayó por el ultimátum de la esposa: "Si me llevas a otro país te mato"
articles.standfirst: Olivier Giroud ha desvelado, aprovechando su 40 cumpleaños, los entresijos familiares de su frustrado traspaso desde el Arsenal al Borussia Dortmund
articles.summary: Olivier Giroud ha desvelado, aprovechando su 40 cumpleaños, los entresijos familiares de su frustrado traspaso desde el Arsenal al Borussia Dortmund
articles.body: Olivier Giroud, el segundo máximo goleador histórico de la selección de Francia con 57 goles (sólo le supera Mbappé con 67 goles), estuvo cerca de fichar por el Borussia Dortmund en 2018 cuando militaba en el Arsenal. En un documental de Canal + para celebrar los 40 años del futbolista el propio Giroud desvela los entresijos de ese fichaje fallido... por culpa de su mujer Jen. En enero de 2018 nació Aaron, el tercero de los cuatros hijos de la pareja Giroud. Olivier Giroud, que actualmente milita en el Lille, relata que cuando le comentó a Jen la posibilidad de fichar por el Borussia Dortmund la respuesta de su mujer fue contundente: "¡Ni lo pienses!. Si ahora me llevas a otro país, a Alemania y encima a Dortmund, entonces te mato". Jen le dejó claro a Olivier que no tenía intención de mudarse de Londres a Alemania. Ante la falta de minutos en el Arsenal y motivado por el deseo de disputar el Mundial de 2018, Giroud acabó fichando por el Chelsea por 17 millones de euros. "En aquel momento, fue una evolución natural. Al final, todo salió bien", recuerda. Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang fue el que finalmente cambió el Arsenal por el Borussia Dortmund. Como jugador del Chelsea entre 2018 y 2021 Giroud disputó 119 partidos en los que marcó 39 goles, repartió 14 asistencias y ganó la Champions League.

articles.title: ‘Is this the end?’ Cristiano Ronaldo’s future with Portugal unclear after veteran star leaves team
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo’s abrupt decision to leave Portugal’s training camp after an apparent rift with coach Jorge Jesus has left many wondering about his future in international soccer.
articles.body: MADRID — Cristiano Ronaldo’s abrupt decision to leave Portugal’s training camp after an apparent rift with coach Jorge Jesus has left many wondering about his future in international soccer. Is he done with Portugal? Or will he make peace with his coach and be back for the next international break? There were few answers on Thursday, a day after the all-time leading scorer in men’s international soccer decided to walk out on Portugal’s training camp in a decision announced a few hours after Jesus said the star forward would not start the game against Denmark in the Nations League. The 41-year-old Ronaldo, who played in his sixth World Cup this year, only said that in due course he would “tell the Portuguese people the truth about the reasons” behind his departure. The federation also gave few details, saying only that Ronaldo left the training camp and the rest of the team would remain focused on Thursday’s game against Denmark. There was already a new holder of Ronaldo’s famous No. 7 jersey, with Rafael Leão set to wear it on Thursday. Because of UEFA rules, Portugal had to assign the number to another player after Ronaldo left the roster. Other players have worn the No. 7 in Ronaldo’s absence in the past. In Portugal, the news of Ronaldo’s departure fueled speculation that the country’s biggest sporting star, who had already hinted that this is his last season in soccer, would not play again for the national team. “Is this the end?” read Thursday’s front-page headline of the JM newspaper based in Ronaldo’s native Madeira. “A sad farewell,” the Portuguese sports paper A Bola said. “CR7 turns his back on the national team,” read the headline on the O Jogo newspaper. Portuguese media also reported that Portugal Prime Minister Luís Montenegro got involved in the situation, having talked individually to Ronaldo, Jesus and soccer federation president Pedro Proença. Possible suspension for Ronaldo? Regardless of Ronaldo’s and the federation’s decisions going forward, the star player could possibly face a harsh punishment for leaving the training camp. The federation’s disciplinary regulations say that any player who “abandons or fails to appear” without justification at a training session, match or activity of the national teams, or any activity related to representing the federation, “shall be sanctioned with a suspension of one to six months,” in addition to a fine. It says the “absence or abandonment shall result in the player’s automatic preventive suspension.” Ronaldo did tell the federation that he was leaving, but it wasn’t clear whether the decision would be considered justified in accordance with the federation’s regulations. Neither the federation nor Ronaldo’s representatives immediately responded to requests for comment by The Associated Press on Thursday. Next steps for the Portugal star Ronaldo reportedly traveled to Madrid, his home for many years while playing for Real Madrid and where he usually stays when not playing with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia. His social media post offered few hints about what’s next. “Following the national team coach’s news conference, and after a conversation with the president of the Portuguese football federation, I decided to leave the national team’s training camp,” Ronaldo said. He ended his message by saying that “now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates.” Many had been expecting Ronaldo to retire from the national team after the World Cup. And while confirmed he wouldn’t appear at another World Cup, he vowed to continue playing and pursuing the milestone of 1,000 career goals. He currently stands at 979, with an international men’s record of 146 goals coming for Portugal. Ronaldo recently said that this Saudi Pro League season is likely to be the last of his professional career. Al-Nassr’s next match is Oct. 9. Coach dismisses talk of a feud with Ronaldo Jesus, who coached Ronaldo at Al-Nassr last season when they won the Saudi Arabian league title together, took over from Roberto Martínez after Portugal’s round-of-16 elimination at the World Cup. He said Wednesday in the pre-game news conference that he was not planning to start Ronaldo in the Nations League match against Denmark. But he dismissed the notion there was a feud between him and Ronaldo, and said the player told him that he would accept any decision he would make. “It seems like there was an issue between us, but there was no issue,” Jesus said before Ronaldo announced his decision to leave. Ronaldo didn’t play Sunday in Portugal’s 2-1 win over Norway. He hadn’t trained with the rest of the group since, sparking widespread rumors about a possible spat with Jesus. The coach said Ronaldo would practice normally on Wednesday, but he ended up deciding to leave. Jesus acknowledged that someone with the stature of Ronaldo deserved a different type of attention from coaches, but emphasized that the “rules are the same for everyone.” Jesus admitted that he told Ronaldo that he would play at least a few minutes against Norway, but changed his mind because of the game’s circumstances. He said he’s the one making the team choices and “no player will ever make a decision for me.” He said it was a mistake to send Ronaldo to warm up for as long as he did, and then not use him against Norway. Jesus added that “any player” would be upset about that. Ronaldo started in Portugal’s 1-0 win over Wales last Thursday but was substituted in the 67th minute. On Tuesday, he posted on Instagram a photo of him wearing the kit accompanied by the country’s flag and a heart emoji.

articles.title: La UAFA cierra filas con Infantino y le ofrece el voto unánime en las elecciones
articles.standfirst: La Unión de Federaciones Árabes de Fútbol, 22 miembros, aplaude los pasos de la FIFA para reforzar la unidad del fútbol mundial y expresa su respaldo al presidente del organismo
articles.summary: La Unión de Federaciones Árabes de Fútbol, 22 miembros, aplaude los pasos de la FIFA para reforzar la unidad del fútbol mundial y expresa su respaldo al presidente del organismo
articles.body: La Unión de Federaciones Árabes de Fútbol (UAFA) ha mostrado este jueves su apoyo a Gianni Infantino al término de la 81ª reunión de su Junta Directiva, celebrada en Yeda y presidida por el príncipe Abdulaziz bin Turki Al-Faisal. En el comunicado final, el organismo árabe recibió con satisfacción las medidas adoptadas recientemente por la FIFA para mantener la colaboración con las federaciones nacionales, regionales y continentales. También valoró los esfuerzos por estrechar la cooperación en las decisiones que buscan hacer crecer el fútbol en todo el mundo. La UAFA, formada por 22 federaciones, fue más allá y reafirmó su respaldo y reconocimiento a Infantino en el próximo periodo. Destacó que, durante más de una década, el presidente de la FIFA ha reforzado la unidad de la comunidad futbolística global, ha desarrollado y expandido el juego y ha ampliado su alcance de un modo que, según el organismo, beneficia a todas las partes implicadas y responde a las aspiraciones de jugadores y aficionados. En el plano interno, la Junta aprobó la formación de los comités de apoyo para el actual mandato 2025-2029. Antes, el secretario general de la UAFA, el doctor Raja Allah Al Sulami, presentó el informe de la Secretaría General, que abarcó asuntos técnicos y administrativos. La Junta analizó además varias iniciativas de desarrollo, entre ellas la llamada Iniciativa Desafío e Innovación. Su objetivo es introducir competiciones de desarrollo que incorporen tecnología moderna en distintos ámbitos del fútbol. Al comienzo de la sesión, el príncipe Abdulaziz bin Turki dio la bienvenida a los miembros de la Junta. Expresó su deseo de que el trabajo conjunto sirva para impulsar y desarrollar el fútbol árabe en todas sus competiciones y actividades.
