articles.title: Andy Robertson: Scotland captain poised for 100th cap
articles.summary: Andy Robertson is poised to become only the second man ever to play 100 times for Scotland. BBC Sport Scotland charts his international career in numbers.
articles.body:
Andy Robertson is poised to become only the second man to win 100 caps for Scotland in more than 150 years of international football.

The national captain could hit the century mark in Saturday's Nations League game against North Macedonia as he closes in on the all-time cap record.

A constant presence since Gordon Strachan handed him his debut in 2014 when he was a fresh-faced left-back with Dundee United, Robertson has defined a generation of the Scotland national team.

Here, BBC Scotland charts the Tottenham Hotspur defender's international career in numbers.

Inside the fairytale journey of Scotland captain Robertson

Robertson set to hit 100 Scotland caps - but who else makes top 10?

The great Kenny Dalglish is the only man to have pulled on the navy blue of Scotland more times than Robertson.

'King Kenny' still tops the list on 102 caps, but that could be eclipsed by his friend come November should the 32-year-old feature in each of Scotland's remaining Nations League games this year.

It is fitting that it will be Robertson who surpasses that long-standing milestone, given the pair have forged a friendship over his time with Liverpool.

"He always says 'you've got millions more games; Nations League, what's that? They didn't have that in my day!'" Robertson joked on the Stick to Football podcast recently.

"I think he might bring up a ratio for years-to-games-played so he's still on top.

"It's obviously something that's been on my radar for a while now. When you get to 80-odd caps, you start to look up."

Dalglish can console himself that his record of 30 goals - held jointly with Denis Law - is safely out of Robertson's reach.

Of current players, John McGinn is lurking only eight behind Robertson on the all-time list, though, so the Scotland men's centurion club could have three members soon.

Since being given the armband by Alex McLeish after Scott Brown retired in 2018, Robertson has captained Scotland 29 times more than any other player.

At the time, he had earned just 22 caps and was just 24 but had established himself as Liverpool's left-back as they reached the Champions League final.

Now, he is the only man to have lead Scotland out at three major finals, reaching the milestone at the World Cup this summer.

Scotland and Napoli midfielder Scott McTominay enthused: "He's such a great captain and he's got that good balance between being one of the senior players and saying you need to wake up if you're not playing well.

"Then he's also got the personable side, organising things with the manager, helping young players and stuff. He's brilliant with that, brilliant."

Robertson has played under four different permanent Scotland team bosses in his 12-year international career.

It was Strachan who plucked him from the under-21s to hand him his debut as a 19-year-old in a win over Poland in March 2014.

McLeish made him captain in 2018, calling Robertson the "outstanding candidate" and an "inspirational figure" - and now he has played twice for new boss Sebastien Pocognoli.

He even played one game under interim manager Malky Mackay in a friendly against the Netherlands at Pittodrie in 2017 as the Scottish FA searched for Strachan's replacement.

However, it is Steve Clarke's seven-year stint that Robertson will be mainly associated with, as the pair lead Scotland to three major tournaments.

Robertson played 68 times for Clarke, all of them as captain, and the recently departed head coach consistently praised his figurehead.

"He's been a fantastic captain for Scotland," Clarke said at the World Cup.

"He's worked ever so hard for the country and he leads the group like the leader he is - and he's very, very important to me and the squad."

Given his longevity, it is perhaps no surprise that Robertson also tops the Scotland assist charts since his debut in 2014.

However, Robertson's rampaging runs and crosses from left-back have been pivotal for a Scotland side that has never been free-scoring during his career.

And, although he only has four Scotland goals, there have been a couple of important ones.

His strike against Cyprus helped ensure the Clarke era started with a win in 2019. And his last-minute winner against Poland in 2024 temporarily staved off Nations League relegation.

That was the last time Robertson scored for Scotland.

Over the piece, Robertson's caps are spread fairly evenly among friendlies and qualification games.

Crucially, though, he has also played nine times in major tournaments. What will rankle with him is there is only one win among those nine - June's victory over Haiti in Boston at the World Cup.

Overall, though, Robertson's Scotland career can be characterised by consistency.

He has started 97 of his 99 caps, and played an average of 83 minutes per game, rarely ever being substituted. He has not missed a camp in three years.

The only question seems to be how many Scotland caps will Robertson end up with? At 32 and still playing in the Premier League, it appears there will be plenty more to come.

articles.title: Man City lodge appeal: Premier League club contest guilty verdict of independent commission
articles.summary: Man City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City have now lodged their appeal against the verdict; City were charged by the Premier League with more than 100 breaches in February 2023
articles.body:
City insist in their statement they are "innocent" and have described the judgement against them as "opinion" and claimed it "contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe".

The independent commission found that between 2009/10 and 2017/18, Man City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m.

The Premier League club had until Friday to appeal and confirmed they had done so in a statement just before midday.

In a statement on Friday, the club said: "Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday 1st October 2026 the club lodged its comprehensive appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter.

"The club's firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case.

"We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete."

The statement from Man City again erroneously refers to a Premier League commission. It is an independent commission.

Analysis: How long will the appeal take?

"The appeal went in on Thursday at 7pm and so, according to the Premier League's rules, the appeal has to be done and dusted in 12 weeks from then, which takes us into the week before Christmas.

"The appeal can only last five days and those five days can only be in one block.

"The appeal panel, which has to be a different three-person panel from the original panel, would have 30 days to make up their minds and deliver their judgement. That would take you into the third week of January.

"Now that is the speeded-up timeline which has been introduced into the Premier League's rules this season.

"Now, Man City could argue that this speeded-up timeline should not apply in this case because this case has been going on for years and this new rule has only been introduced this season. That is something to look out for."

Details of Man City's appeal strategy explained

Latest from Sky Sports News' Lyall Thomas :

Manchester City are likely to argue as part of their appeal that the extra funding for their sponsorship deals came from the Abu Dhabi government rather than the club's owners, Sky Sports News understands.

City's lawyers argued during the 2024 hearing that the funding had come from the Abu Dhabi government, but this was rejected by the independent commission, which "concluded it was an explanation that the club had concocted well after the event in an attempt to conceal the realities of the Disguised Funding Scheme".

However, it is understood City are expected to continue contesting this argument.

Manchester City is majority owned by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan's Newton Investment and Development LLC. Sheikh Mansour is also a member of the ruling family of Abu Dhabi and he is the vice-president and deputy prime minister of the United Arab Emirates.

The separation of UAE state investment and those that are private from the Abu Dhabi royal family has long been a subject of debate and criticism.

What did the independent commission find?

Manchester City arranged "sham" contracts with a number of its commercial partners as part of a "disguised funding scheme" to artificially inflate the club's revenues by £830m.

The club filed accounts that concealed the true state of its finances.

Manchester City were significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits and broke "well over 100" Premier League regulations.

Manchester City failed to co-operate and act in good faith towards the league during the investigation, with three out of four alleged breaches upheld and one charge not proven

The commission also said it was "regrettable" that a decision had taken so long to reach, with the hearing having taken place between September and December 2024.

Following the publication of the guilty verdict, a Manchester City statement released on Tuesday read: "Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League commission, that has been published today.

"The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.

"The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."

As above, Manchester City's statement erroneously refers to a Premier League commission. It is an independent commission.

Why Man City's appeal could drag into 2027

Latest from Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol and Amar Mehta :

Manchester City's appeal could drag on into next year if they argue that the process should not be run according to Premier League rules which were introduced for this season.

City have filed their appeal and the new rules about appeals state that this part of the disciplinary process has to be concluded within 12 weeks and the appeal hearing can last no longer than five days.

City's lawyers could argue that they were charged in 2023 and a hearing was held in 2024 - when the rules about a speeded-up appeals process were not in the Premier League Handbook.

A legal expert told Sky Sports News Manchester City would have a strong case for arguing that the new rules should not apply in this case.

The new rules were introduced to ensure that clubs, where possible, were punished in the same season as relevant rule breaches.

articles.title: Turkey's football referee chief faces judge in graft probe
articles.summary: The head of Turkey's football refereeing body and six others were due in court on Friday, three days after being detained as part of a graft investigation, m...
articles.body:
The head of Turkey's football refereeing body and six others were due in court on Friday, three days after being detained as part of a graft investigation, media reports said.

Ferhat Gundogdu, head of the Central Referees Committee (MHK), and six others were detained on Tuesday as part of a probe into allegations of top-level manipulation of the referee administration process.

They were to appear before a judge at Istanbul's Caglayan courthouse on several charges, including "official document forgery", "breach of trust" and "illegal acquisition of personal data".

As part of the same probe by prosecutors with the illegal betting and sports crime unit, police also detained Yasin Kol, a referee from Turkey's top-flight Super Lig, as well as an assistant referee, media reports said.

"I haven't placed any bets. I just sent money to a few people I care about who asked me to lend them money," Kol said in remarks relayed by IHA news agency.

Another report in the Cumhuriyet daily said investigators were examining a list of referees shared between Gundogdu and the head of the Turkish Football Federation (TFF), Ibrahim Haciosmanoglu.

Ayhan Sensoy, a sports journalist who wrote a 2024 book on the issue called "The Gambling Pit", told AFP it was unlikely that the federation bosses "have any chance of staying in office".

Although the next TFF presidential election was due in June 2027, "it seems like they may announce a decision to hold an extraordinary general assembly within the next few days", Sensoy added.

For now, the TFF administration is in Liege for Friday's UEFA Nations League match against Belgium, but Sensoy said they were likely to make an announcement on their return to Turkey on Saturday.

On Tuesday, Justice Minister Akin Gurlek said that prosecutors were examining claims about "interference in the processes of referee classification, assignments, scoring and appointments, as well as the exams on rules".

"We will steadfastly continue the fight for clean football so... those responsible are held accountable," Gurlek said.

During the raids, police searched the VAR room at the TFF's headquarters in Riva on the Asian side of Istanbul.

Although the TFF made no mention of the arrests at the time, it issued a statement on Wednesday denying claims some material had been deleted before the police arrived.

"Allegations that digital materials in the relevant units of the Turkish Football Federation were deleted before the inspection, and that the deleted materials were recovered by police technical personnel are completely unfounded," it said.

One leaked document pointed to an exchange in which Super Lig referee Kol sent Gundogdu a list of referees, writing: "Chairman, whatever you think works."

Samil Tayyar, a journalist and lawmaker with the ruling AKP, said the exchange was very revealing.

"Football is not just a spectator sport. It is an industry where billions of dollars circulate" and the exchange between these two men should be read "with this perspective in mind," he wrote on X.

During last year's referee scandal, a TFF investigation found 371 of Turkey's 571 referees officiating in the professional leagues had betting accounts and 152 of them actively placed bets.

But they only faced disciplinary measures.

"It does seem to be a continuation of 2025, and it looks like it will continue further," Sensoy told AFP, saying the scandal would soon expose "second- and third-division club presidents, as well as club executives and club owners".

"Unfortunately, Turkey has experienced a serious wave of illegal betting over the past 10 years.. It's a serious problem."

articles.title: Costa: "El perfeccionismo es una mierda, pero el inconformismo es muy importante"
articles.standfirst: El técnico ha recalcado que todo lo que ha hecho el Sabadell hasta ahora no sirve de nada
articles.summary: El técnico ha recalcado que todo lo que ha hecho el Sabadell hasta ahora no sirve de nada
articles.body: El Sabadell, equipo revelación de este inicio de curso en Segunda división, es séptimo tras siete jornadas, pero Ferran Costa, su entrenador, insiste en la necesidad de "no fliparse" cada vez que se pone delante de un micrófono y en la importancia de encontrar un equilibrio entre la alegría y la exigencia. "Debemos mejorar en absolutamente todo, pero forma parte de nuestra esencia. El perfeccionismo es una mierda, pero el inconformismo es muy importante. Es lo que nos mueve a trabajar valientes, a apretar el culo, a ponernos cada día a cero. Es lo que marca nuestro camino, nuestra hoja de ruta", ha recalcado este viernes. El míster ha celebrado la "identidad" y la "estabilidad" que transmite el equipo en cada partido, pero ha vuelto pedir calma, pies en el suelo: "Lo que has hecho no sirve de nada porque lo único que importa es lo que pasa desde que pita el árbitro". Este sábado su Sabadell se enfrentará al Andorra, su exequipo, pero Costa ha enfatizado que será un partido como cualquier otro, una tarde más. "Lo único diferente de esta semana es que he estado con migrañas, porque cuando llueve me coge un dolor de cabeza de cojones", ha subrayado el joven técnico arlequinado, una fuente inagotable de titulares. Su homólogo, Carles Manso, había dicho unos minutos antes que el partido sería una guerra por la intensidad del Sabadell, pero Costa ha restado trascendencia a la contienda. "No creo que la palabra guerra se ajuste a un partido de fútbol. Iremos a cada pelota como si fuera la última porque es nuestra esencia, pero nada más allá de esto". También ha reivindicado que el equipo sigue demostrando que es competitivo y difícil de batir incluso en los partidos más discretos, como el empate de la última jornada contra el Celta Fortuna en Vigo (1-1). "No estuvimos a un nivel tan alto como en otros partidos. No estuvimos finos a nivel de vistosidad, a nivel técnico. Un error importante de los que no nos podemos permitir nos costó un gol en el minuto 5, pero el equipo se recompuso, empatamos y jugamos toda la segunda parte en campo contrario, fuera de casa y contra un equipo con mucho talento", ha reivindicado.

articles.title: Leipzig keen to open talks with Raum over expiring contract as Barcelona and Juventus circle
articles.summary: David Raum’s future at RB Leipzig remains up in the air, with the club captain’s current deal set to expire at the end of the season.According to Sky Germany...
articles.body:
David Raum's future at RB Leipzig remains up in the air, with the club captain's current deal set to expire at the end of the season.

According to Sky Germany, Leipzig would like to keep the 28-year-old and are planning to open talks with him over a potential contract extension in the coming weeks.

However, the left-back's salary could prove to be a sticking point. Raum is reportedly currently Leipzig's second-highest earner, behind only Lukas Klostermann, and would have to adjust his demands to fit the club's new salary structure.

Whether the two parties will be able to reach an agreement remains unclear, with the likes of Barcelona and Juventus recently linked with the Germany international.

Raum joined Die Roten Bullen from TSG Hoffenheim for a reported €26 million fee in 2022.

articles.title: Una prueba ante el Santa Clara para cerrar la semana
articles.standfirst: Los célticos jugaron un partidillo a puerta cerrada ante los portugueses
articles.summary: Los célticos jugaron un partidillo a puerta cerrada ante los portugueses
articles.body: El Celta cerró esta semana de entrenamientos con un partidillo, a puerta cerrada en la Ciudad Deportiva Afouteza, ante el Santa Clara, cuarto clasificado en la liga portuguesa, por detrás de los tres grandes, y cuyo máximo goleador es el ex céltico Gonçalo Paciencia. El equipo de Claudio Giráldez buscó un oponente en el país vecino que sirviese para trabajar diferentes conceptos tácticos y tener activos a sus futbolistas, fundamentalmente a los que menos participación han tenido en el arranque liguero o las últimas incorporaciones que no hayan viajado con sus selecciones. Este parón ha servido para poner a punto a Borja Iglesias, que a la vuelta ya podrá disponer de minutos de inicio en los partidos, o recuperar físicamente a Aleix Febas. En el partidillo no pudieron participar los cinco internacionales que siguen fuera de Vigo ni los lesionados Miguel Román, Sebastián Cáceres, Iago Aspas y Jones El-Abdellaoui. La plantilla descansará el fin de semana para arrancar la próxima con la vista puesta en la reanudación de la competición liguera en Elche.
